hints: Set up the chord gradient formula $\frac{y_B - y_A}{(2+h) - 2} = \frac{f(2+h) - 5}{h}$.
Expand the numerator, factor out $h$, and simplify.
walkthrough:
Find the $y$-coordinates of points $A$ and $B$ on the curve $y = 2x^2 - 3$:
$$y_A = f(2) = 2(2)^2 - 3 = 5$$
$$y_B = f(2+h) = 2(2+h)^2 - 3 = 2(4 + 4h + h^2) - 3 = 5 + 8h + 2h^2$$

Apply the chord gradient formula $m_{AB} = \frac{y_B - y_A}{(2+h) - 2}$:
$$m_{AB} = \frac{(5 + 8h + 2h^2) - 5}{h} = \frac{8h + 2h^2}{h}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiation from First Principles: Evaluates $f(2+h) = 2(2+h)^2-3$ (B1). Sets up chord gradient $\frac{2h^2+8h}{h}$ (M1). Obtains simplified expression $2h+8$ (A1).

hints: Explain that as $h \to 0$, the chord $AB$ approaches the tangent to the curve at $A$.
walkthrough:
Explain the geometric limiting process:
$$\text{As } h \to 0, \text{ point } B \text{ approaches point } A \text{ along the curve, so the chord } AB \text{ tends to the tangent at } A.$$

State the value of the gradient of the curve at $A$ by taking the limit:
$$\text{Gradient at } A = \lim_{h \to 0} (2h + 8) = 8$$

ai_rubric.Differentiation from First Principles: States that $h \to 0$ or chord $AB \to$ tangent at $A$ (B1). States gradient value $8$ (B1).
